question: Which of the following triangles cannot exist?
solution:
A right triangle has one \(90^\circ\) angle. Its other two positive angles must therefore add to \(90^\circ\), so each is acute. Thus a right triangle cannot also have an obtuse angle.

The other combinations do occur. For A, B, D, and E, respective examples of angle triples are \((70^\circ,70^\circ,40^\circ)\), \((45^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ)\), \((30^\circ,60^\circ,90^\circ)\), and \((20^\circ,40^\circ,120^\circ)\). Equal angles give equal opposite sides, while three different angles give three different sides.

The triangle that cannot exist is an obtuse right triangle, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

nodes.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent ; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.
nodes.label: G-CO.C.10

placement.meaning: High school band, not an exact year

nodes.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles. For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.
nodes.label: 8.G.A.5

nodes.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent ; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent ; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment’s endpoints.
nodes.label: G-CO.C.9

placement.meaning: High school band, not an exact year

nodes.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.
nodes.label: 8.G.A.2

nodes.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions .
nodes.label: G-CO.B.8

placement.meaning: High school band, not an exact year

nodes.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations ; given two similar two- dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

edges.scope: Classifying the triangle by its angles and identifying equal-side special cases

edges.reason: The theorem's three quantities are the triangle's interior angles, requiring that geometric object and its elements.
The same explicit three-lines property includes the altitude, so perpendicular altitude meaning is a component.
The same explicit three-lines property includes the median, so median and side-midpoint meanings are components.
The target expressly says the apex-angle bisector coincides with the median and altitude; angle-bisector meaning is needed to state that coincidence.
The equal-angle-to-equal-side criterion can be proved independently by a bisector and AAS. Its forward counterpart is helpful comparison, not an explicit comparison criterion in this target.
The acute/right/obtuse classification uses angle size and degree units, including the ninety- and one-hundred-eighty-degree thresholds.
